chapter: The Legends of Jazz and life on the road
title: South Frisco Jazz Band and Club New Orleans
summary: He plays weekends in Huntington Beach with the white South Frisco Jazz Band, opening at Club New Orleans on election night 1972.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: During that time I was working with a white band from Huntington Beach, called the South Frisco Jazz Band and I worked out there six months with them just weekends.
In Huntington Beach, a pizza parlor.
You drove from Pasadena down to Huntington Beach?

That's right, for six months, every Friday and Saturday night. Later on that year they got a job at a nightclub called Club New Orleans, / and I stayed with them for eight months. While we were there--this is 1972--right after I left the senior citizens, our first night out there was the night that Nixon got elected, there was a special party that night, an election night party they called it. 1972,
This was after you were no longer a host at the senior citizens?
That's right. That was our opening night and we stayed there on that job from November to June, eight months.
